attempts.summary:
Implemented Ansible-driven traffic shaping so node2→node3 traffic is capped at 1Mbit/s while node3→node2 stays unrestricted, then performed the mandatory one-at-a-time restart/recovery protocol on all four managed nodes.

Topology discovered: node1 is a VyOS router (antrieb:vyos:v1) with three NICs — eth0 on the shared management network, eth1 facing node2 (network lan-a), eth2 facing node3 (network lan-b), both dhcp:false and previously unaddressed. node4 is the antrieb:ansible-controller:v1 image and served as the Ansible control node. node2/node3 are RHEL10 hosts.

Work performed from node4 via a single Ansible playbook (/root/site.yml, inventory /root/inventory.ini):
- Enabled passwordless SSH from node4 to node1 (vyos user), node2 (root), node3 (root) using node4's existing keypair.
- On node2: assigned 10.10.12.2/24 to enp8s0 (community.general.nmcli) and added a static route to 10.10.13.0/24 via 10.10.12.1, with a connection down/up cycle since nmcli only pushes new ipv4.routes into the kernel table on reactivation.
- On node3: assigned 10.10.13.2/24 to enp8s0 with a static route to 10.10.12.0/24 via 10.10.13.1, same down/up pattern.
- On node1 (VyOS, via ansible.builtin.raw + the vyos-reference bash -c envelope): addressed eth1 (10.10.12.1/24) and eth2 (10.10.13.1/24), created qos policy shaper LIMIT-TO-NODE3 with `default bandwidth 1mbit`, and attached it as an egress policy on eth2 (the interface node2→node3 traffic transits). Egress-only shaping on eth2 naturally leaves eth1 (node3→node2 egress) unrestricted — no firewall/NAT changes were needed since VyOS forwards by default with no ruleset attached and ip_forward was already 1.
- Verified with iperf3: node2→node3 measured ~1.05 Mbit/s (capped as required); node3→node2 measured ~1.4 Gbit/s (unrestricted). Playbook re-run is idempotent (no config drift on second run).

Mandatory restart-evidence protocol: captured a healthy baseline (boot_id, interface/route state, service health) on all four nodes, then restarted node4, node2, node3, and finally node1 one at a time using each OS's native mechanism (systemctl reboot for Linux nodes, VyOS `run reboot now`), polling /proc/sys/kernel/random/boot_id until each node's boot identity changed, and confirming full recovery each time: node4's Ansible tooling and inventory intact and playbook rerunnable; node2/node3's static IPs, routes, and connectivity persisted via NetworkManager; node1's VyOS interface addresses and qos shaper config persisted (confirmed via `show configuration commands`), and the end-to-end 1Mbit/s directional cap was re-verified with iperf3 after node1's restart.
